title: Etale lifting of a split torus subgroup at an algebraically closed residue field
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $s\in S$ have algebraically closed residue field $k=\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. An $S$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with $S$ in place of the field base. Write $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal O_S[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units, and $\mathbf G_{m,S}^0=1_S$. Let $r\geq0$ and let $j_0:\mathbf G_{m,k}^r\hookrightarrow G_s$ be a closed subgroup immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There exist a commutative $A$-algebra $C$, an affine etale morphism $p:U=\operatorname{Spec}C\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $p(u)=s$ and $\kappa(u)=k$ via $p$, and a closed subgroup immersion $j:\mathbf G_{m,U}^r\hookrightarrow G\times_S U$ whose fibre at $u$ is $j_0$ under this residue-field identification. No reductivity or connectedness of $G$ and no henselian hypothesis on $A$ is required.

source.place: WANTED locally; Brian Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Proposition 3.1.6, printed pp.83-84, and Proposition B.3.4, printed pp.290-292: etale lifting of the multiplicative type subgroup followed by etale splitting, at a point with algebraically closed residue field; read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}H$. The affine smoothness equivalence identifies $A\to H$ as a smooth ring map. By the smooth-algebra finite-type model theorem, the smooth $A$-algebra $H$ descends to a smooth finitely presented $A_i$-algebra $H_i$, with $A_i\subset A$ a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra. Enlarge $A_i$ to descend the group structure as well: the comultiplication, counit and antipode are specified on finitely many algebra generators, and their defining identities are finitely many equalities on these generators. The finite-data lemma descends their coefficients and the finite polynomial witnesses for those equalities to one subalgebra. Thus $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}H_i$ is a smooth affine group with $G_i\times_{A_i}A\simeq G$. Smoothness is retained because every enlargement replaces $H_i$ by its scalar extension.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84, initial finite-type reduction; affine finite-coefficient elaboration using Stacks Tags 00TP and 05N9

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ correspond to $s$ and $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak p\cap A_i$. As the finitely generated subrings containing our model vary, the fields $k_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i/\mathfrak p_i)$ are nested subfields with union $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$. Apply finite-presentation algebra-map descent to the coordinate map of $j_0$, with target $k[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1}]$, to obtain $j_i:\mathbf G_{m,k_i}^r\to(G_i)_{k_i}$ at one stage. The same lemma's equality clause, applied to comultiplication, counit and antipode on the finitely many algebra generators, ensures that $j_i$ is a group homomorphism. Apply closed-immersion descent to this morphism along $\operatorname{Spec}k=\varprojlim\operatorname{Spec}k_i$, enlarging the stage once more, to make $j_i$ a closed immersion. Its scalar extension is the specified map $j_0$, not just a subgroup isomorphic to its image. All schemes in this application are affine of finite presentation over their field, hence qcqs, and the initial morphism is locally of finite type.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84, initial finite-type reduction; Stacks Tags 05N9 (2)-(3), 01ZP

proof.text: Put $R=(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and $\widehat R=\varprojlim R/(\mathfrak p_iR)^n$. The excellence of $\mathbf Z$ and stability of excellence under finite type and localization make both $A_i$ and $R$ excellent; by its definition they are Noetherian G-rings. The completion lemmas make $\widehat R$ Noetherian and local with residue field $k_i$ and maximal ideal $(\mathfrak p_iR)\widehat R$. Applied to $M=R$ and the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak p_iR$, the module-completion theorem makes $\widehat R$ complete for this maximal ideal. This verifies every base-ring hypothesis of the complete-local lifting lemma.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84, passage to the completed local ring; Stacks Tags 07QW, 07QU, 07QT, 0316, 05GI, 05GG

proof.text: The base change $G_i\times_{A_i}\widehat R$ is smooth. Apply the complete-local split-torus homomorphism lifting lemma to $j_i$ to obtain a closed subgroup homomorphism $\widehat j:\mathbf G_{m,\widehat R}^r\hookrightarrow G_i\times_{A_i}\widehat R$ reducing exactly to $j_i$. Write $\widehat R$ as the directed union of its finitely generated $A_i$-subalgebras $B_\alpha$. The torus and $G_i$ are fixed affine finitely presented models. Finite-presentation algebra-map descent, followed by its equality clause for the three Hopf-map identities, descends $\widehat j$ to a group homomorphism $j_B$ over some $B=B_\alpha$. Closed-immersion descent makes $j_B$ closed after increasing $\alpha$. The systems here have affine qcqs bases; both source and target are finitely presented over each base, so the morphism to which closed-immersion descent is applied is locally of finite type. The residue map $B\hookrightarrow\widehat R\to k_i$ identifies its fibre with $j_i$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84, lifting by Corollary B.3.5 and descent to a finite type subalgebra of the completion

proof.text: Since $A_i$ is Noetherian and $B$ is a finite type $A_i$-algebra, write $B=A_i[z_1,\ldots,z_N]/(F_1,\ldots,F_M)$ using finite-type-to-finite-presentation. The inclusion $B\to\widehat R$ is a solution of these finitely many equations. Apply Artin approximation over $A_i$ at $\mathfrak p_i$, with precision $1$: its hypotheses hold because $A_i$ is Noetherian and $(A_i)_{\mathfrak p_i}=R$ is a G-ring. It gives an etale $A_i$-algebra $A'_i$, a point $u_i$ over $\mathfrak p_i$ with residue field $k_i$, and a map $B\to A'_i$ whose reduction to $k_i$ is the given residue map. Pulling $j_B$ back by this map gives a closed group homomorphism over $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A'_i$. Its fibre at $u_i$ is $j_i$: agreement modulo the maximal ideal on the generators $z_a$ implies agreement on every element of $B$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6 and Theorem 3.1.7, printed p.84; precise approximation formulation Stacks Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), with N=1

proof.text: Set $C=A\otimes_{A_i}A'_i$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}C= S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_i}U_i$. Etale base-change stability makes $U\to S$ etale; it is affine because it is induced by this ring map. The base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k_i\to U_i$ along $s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}k$, since $k\otimes_{k_i}k_i=k$. It defines a point $u$ over $s$ with residue field exactly $k$. Pull back the closed subgroup homomorphism from step 5 to $U$; closed-immersion base-change stability gives the required $j$. Its fibre at $u$ is $(j_i)_k=j_0$ by step 2. The split source remains $\mathbf G_{m,U}^r$ throughout. Rank zero uses the same empty-product construction; the argument imposes no connectedness, reductivity or henselian condition on the original base.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.6, printed p.84, return by base change from the finite-type model; no separate torus splitting is needed

lean.note: The neighbourhood is encoded by C and p: Spec C → Spec A, equivalent to an A-algebra by Spec.homEquiv. The point is q: Spec κ(s) → Spec C with q ≫ p the canonical residue point and an isomorphism on residue fields. The tori are pullbacks of the existing relativeSplitTorus over Spec A; the final equality uses the canonical pullback map and projection to G to specify precisely the fibre embedding.
